description: Make the arm swappable too. Bring in the SO-101 arm's CAD (official TheRobotStudio/SO-ARM100 repo has SO-101 STEP/STL files; record the source URL and license) as a new Arm version, Arm 2, converted for the live preview. Then design a new Mount version that attaches our latest custom gripper base to the SO-101's wrist, replacing its stock gripper/jaw: match the SO-101 wrist bolt pattern and the STS3215 wrist servo horn. In the live preview Jake can switch between arms (Arm 1 reBot B601-RS, Arm 2 SO-101) the same way he switches grippers and mounts, with each mount's compatibility flagged per arm. Keep it parameterized and printable without supports. Related pebbles: per-part picker voice-a5d65841, Base 14 voice-4ac7222b (STS3215 base on the arm), STS3215 variant voice-e82254ec.

results.identified_issue: Mount 2 = new hub only (v315 is a copy of v314 with hub() replaced; Base 14 parts byte-identical geometry, so no Base bump). Horn face = stock fixed jaw's flat seat at gripper_link z -3.0, screw circle centred x -0.7 (URDF roll axis 0.7 mm off the jaw's holes; hub follows the jaw). Collar of wrist_roll_pitch: r>=15.2, min z -4.7 -> neck r 12.5, so_neck_h 3.5. Pose UPRIGHT=(0,0.6,-1.1,-1.0708,0) chosen by eye. so101_pose.py imports FK helpers from rebot arm_pose.py (renamed apart to avoid module clash). Publisher: own_part() lets a folder lead with 'Mount 2 (…), Arm 2' -> 'Mount 2 assembly' row + carried Mount 2/Arm 2; tool_plate field from "Mount 1's tool plate" in the entry; gallery mixFlags accepts mount.design.tool_plate. Aero–Arm flag left strict (Aero assembly positioned for Arm 1). Known: Mount 1/Arm 1 exported in Base 10's frame are offset from Base 14 in the mix (pre-existing). test_gripper_poses fails on v306 (no poses.js entry at HEAD; pre-existing, untouched).
results.summary: The SO-101 is now Arm 2, and a new Mount 2 holds our gripper on its wrist. In the live preview you can switch between the reBot and the SO-101. Mount 2 is a hub on the SO-101's wrist-roll horn, and Mount 1's tool plate fits over it, so Base 14 goes on either arm unchanged.
results.detailed_description:
Arm 2 is The Robot Studio's own SO-101 follower model, from the SO-ARM100 repo (pinned commit a758567, Apache-2.0). Its URDF and meshes are in cad/arm/so101/, along with the source link, the licence and a script that poses the arm for the preview.

Mount 2 is one new printed part that takes the place of the SO-101's stock fixed jaw. The stock jaw screws to the wrist-roll servo's horn with 4 M3 on Ø14, and the hub uses those same 4 holes, with countersunk M3×6 from the top. A shallow socket round the Ø20 horn centres it. The SO-101's wrist part has a collar round the horn, so the hub narrows to a Ø25 neck that turns inside it. Above the neck, the outside is exactly Mount 1's hub. So Mount 1's tool plate slides over it and locks with the same 3 side screws. That means Base 14, Base 10 or the Aero Hand plate fit either arm. Base 14 is unchanged; the folder v315_generalist_so101_mount is the Mount 2 assembly, not a new Base. Every hub dimension is a slider in params.json (the neck, the socket, the screw length and how far it threads into the horn). It prints tool face down with no supports.

In the preview, the Arm picker now has Arm 1 (reBot) and Arm 2 (SO-101), and the Mount picker has Mount 1 and Mount 2. Pick a mismatch and you get a warning, for example "Mount 2 fits Arm 2, not Arm 1". A Base fits any Mount that takes the tool plate it was built for. All 89 geometry checks pass. They include: the hub seats on the horn and is centred by it; the screws stop inside the 2.5 mm horn; the SO-101 stays clear of everything that rolls with the wrist, at any roll angle.

What isn't verified: I measured the horn, the collar and the bolt pattern from The Robot Studio's meshes, not from a real SO-101. The gripper is heavier than the stock jaw and hangs on a plastic horn, and nothing has been load-tested. One gap in the preview: Mount 1 and Arm 1 come from Base 10's export, so they sit lower than Base 14 when you combine them (that was already true before this change). The routing of the jaw servo's cable isn't modelled either. Next: open the Generalist mix with Arm 2 + Mount 2 + Base 14.

summary: Add the SO-101 arm CAD from the official SO-ARM100 repo (recording source URL and license) as swappable Arm 2 in the live preview, plus a new Mount that fits its wrist. The mount must replace the stock jaw, match the SO-101 bolt pattern and STS3215 horn, be parameterized and support-free printable, and flag each mount's compatibility per arm.
